chunks: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir said:

He said: The punishment for the Jew, the Christian, and the slave for drinking wine and for slander is the same. And the People of the Covenant were settled upon the condition that they drink it in their houses.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: Wine (specifically for the hadd of drinking)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for Jews, Christians, and slaves for drinking wine according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies that the fixed legal punishments (hadd) for drinking wine and slander apply equally to Jews, Christians, and slaves, rejecting any exemption based on status or religion. It highlights a specific juristic nuance for the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah), noting that their agreement (sulh) permits them to consume wine privately within their homes, distinguishing their internal practice from the public application of the hadd. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of how dhimmi contracts interact with Islamic penal law.
